main_text.head: DE SUPER-BIA.
main_text.p: SUperbia est, aliorum omnium praeter quam ui, contemtus. Homo uperbus talis est. Si quis cum properè conventum velit, à cœna se illum cō-veniturum dicet inter am-bulandum. Si fuerit de quoquam bene meritus, neminisse beneficij etiam n viis iubebit, atq; adeo oget. Prior ad quem-quā accedere nolet. Eos qui emūt aliquid ab ipso, vel aliquid rerum illius conduxerunt, iubere non eretur, vt prima luce ad e veniant. Dum per vias ingreditur, caput semper demittens, obviorum ne-minem alloquitur. Si vi-ùm aliquando ei fuerit, amicos convivio excipe-Ἔστι ἡ ὑπερφανία καὶ καταφρόνησις τῆς πλὴν αὐτοῦ τῶν ἄλλων. Ὁ δὲ ὑπερήφανος τοὺς δὲ τὰς, οἷος τῷ ἀσθενοῦντι ὑπὸ * δείπνε ἐν ἰδ[?] φάγειν ἐν τῷ ὠφελι- * παίειν. ἡ δὲ ποιήσας, μεμνῆσθαι φάσκειν ἐν τῇ ὁδοῖς, ἡ βιάζειν. ἡ περιελθεῖν πρότερον ἐδενὶ ζελήσας. καὶ τὲς πολεῖτας ἡ μεμιδωμένους δέ- νος κελόσαν ἡκειν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀμὶ ἡμέρα. ἡ ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς προδύμου μὴ λα- λεῖν τοῖς ἐντυγχάνε- σι, ἡ ἀπὸ κεκυφώς. ὅταν δὲ αὐτῷ δόξῃ ἐσᾶν τὰς φίλας, ἀυ- τὸς μὴ σωφρονεῖν,

te, ipse cū illis non cænat.

page.notes: Column edges at the left are cropped, so several lines begin with a partial word (e.g. "ui", "uperbus", "oget", "eretur"); these are given as far as they are visible. The Greek running head and the italic Greek line are read with some doubt. "vi-ùm" is printed with a grave accent and is kept as printed; the sense suggests "vi-um". Greek column is read from a difficult scan; several words are doubtful and marked [?]. The asterisks in the right margin are reference marks with no printed note text beside them. The Latin line at the lower left is a fragment and stays as printed. The large initial E opens the first word.
